ampelosaurus:enwiki:4.title: Ampelosaurus (Purported Ampelosaurus remains from other localities)

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, specifically the Early Maastrichtian epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, (Early Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: The type species of Ampelosaurus is A. atacis, which was named by Jean Le Loeuff in 1995.
facts.quote: Its type species is A. atacis, named by Le Loeuff in 1995.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus possessed a long neck and tail like other sauropods and was covered in armor made of osteoderms.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus would have had a long neck and tail — like most sauropods — but it also carried armor in the form of osteoderms.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ampelosaurus date to approximately 71.5 million years ago, corresponding to the early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Its remains were found in a level dating from 71.5 million years ago, representing the early Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The largest known individual of Ampelosaurus reached a length of about 14 meters, making it too large to be considered an insular dwarf despite living on an island environment.
facts.quote: However, with a size of about 14 m in length for the largest known individual, Ampelosaurus was not an insular dwarf unlike some other Ibero-Armorican titanosaurs like Lirainosaurus and Atsinganosaurus, or the genus Magyarosaurus from the Hateg island.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus inhabited the Ibero-Armorican Island, a landmass that included much of modern-day France and the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus lived on what was the Ibero-Armorican Island, a landmass including much of present-day France and Iberian Peninsula.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus remains were recovered from the lower levels of the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation, dating to approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was recovered in the lower levels of the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation, which belong to the early Maastrichtian epoch of the Late Cretaceous Period, ~ 70 million years ago.

facts.statement: The dinosaur was formally named Ampelosaurus atacis by French paleontologist Jean Le Loeuff in a preliminary description published in 1995.
facts.quote: This new dinosaur was named Ampelosaurus atacis by the French paleontologist Jean Le Loeuff in a preliminary description published in 1995.

facts.statement: The name Ampelosaurus means "vineyard lizard," derived from Greek and Latin roots referencing the Blanquette de Limoux vineyard where it was found.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus is derived from the Greek αμπελος, "the vine" and the Latinised Greek saurus, "reptile". Therefore, Ampelosaurus means "vineyard lizard" after the Blanquette de Limoux vineyard.

facts.statement: Remains of a larger Ampelosaurus specimen were discovered in 2007, including a 1.20-meter femur and other skeletal elements.
facts.quote: In 2007, the remains of a larger specimen were discovered, including a sternal plate, a scapula, a 1.20 m femur, a pubis, a caudal vertebra and a chevron.

facts.statement: A 2012 study suggested that Bellevue contained three morphotypes of titanosaurs, with one tentatively assigned to the genus Lirainosaurus, creating debate over species attribution.
facts.quote: However, in 2012, a morphometric study of titanosaur femurs from France and Spain suggested the presence of three morphotypes at Bellevue, one of which was tentatively assigned to the genus Lirainosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers in 2021 agreed that a second titanosaur species existed at Bellevue but suggested it was more similar to the genus Garrigatitan.
facts.quote: In 2021, Díez Díaz and colleagues also agree on the existence at this site of a second titanosaur but find it more similar to the genus Garrigatitan from the Upper Campanian of Provence.

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate that the diagnosis of Ampelosaurus will need to be revised due to the presence of additional titanosaur species at the site.
facts.quote: This study will also lead to an emended diagnosis of Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: Reports of Ampelosaurus remains in the Petites Pyrénées and Chaînon de Saint-Chinian have never been confirmed by a formal publication.
facts.quote: However this has never been confirmed by a publication.

facts.statement: Studies have shown that titanosaur teeth found at Cruzy differ from those of Ampelosaurus and belong to a new taxon currently under description.
facts.quote: A later study showed that Cruzy's titanosaur teeth are different from those of Ampelosaurus, and belong to a new taxon whose description is in progress.

facts.statement: In 2019, researchers reclassified a braincase previously attributed to Ampelosaurus as belonging to Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, a species described in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2019, Knoll and colleagues finally referred this braincase to Lohuecotitan pandafilandi, which was described in 2016 from a postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus possessed armor made of osteoderms ranging from 25 to 28 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Like most sauropods, Ampelosaurus would have had a long neck and tail, but it also carried armor in the form of osteoderms 25 to 28 cm long.

facts.statement: The osteoderms found on Ampelosaurus exhibited three distinct shapes: plates, bulbs, and spines.
facts.quote: The four osteoderms found have three different morphologies, they are plate, bulb, and spine-shaped.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 15 to 16 meters and a body mass of approximately 8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus is thought to have measured 15 - 16 m in length and about 8 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: A 2022 study assigned a length of 13.9 meters and a weight of 9.98 metric tons to the largest known individual of Ampelosaurus based on femur measurements.
facts.quote: In 2022, Vila and colleagues assign a size of 13.9 m long and a weight of 9.98 MT for the largest individual based on the femur MDE-C3-174 (Vila et al. Supplementary Information).

facts.statement: The species Ampelosaurus atacis is known from numerous unattached bones and teeth.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus atacis is known from many unattached bones and teeth.

facts.statement: Coria and colleagues classified Ampelosaurus as a dwarf sauropod in 2005 due to its smaller size relative to its ancestors.
facts.quote: It is considered to be a dwarf sauropod by Coria et al. (2005) because it has a smaller size in comparison with its ancestors.

facts.statement: Klein and colleagues argued in 2012 that Ampelosaurus was not an insular dwarf because its adult size exceeded that of Europasaurus and Magyarosaurus.
facts.quote: However, according to Klein et al. (2012), Ampelosaurus is not an insular dwarf since its adult size is much greater than that of Europasaurus or Magyarosaurus.

facts.statement: Over 500 bones discovered since 1989 at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality in southern France have been assigned to Ampelosaurus atacis.
facts.quote: Since 1989, over 500 bones discovered at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality of southern France have been assigned to A. atacis.

facts.statement: By 2023, the count of dinosaur bones known from Bellevue had risen to 1,400, mostly titanosaurs that likely represent at least two species.
facts.quote: In 2023 Vila and colleagues increased this number to 1400 dinosaur bones known at Bellevue, the majority belonging to titanosaurs, likely including at least two species.

facts.statement: A partially articulated skeleton nicknamed "Eva" was found in 2001, but it has not yet been formally described.
facts.quote: In 2001 a partially articulated skeleton was found, including a disarticulated skull. This specimen, nicknamed "Eva", has not yet been described.

facts.statement: Le Loeuff provided a complete description of all known Ampelosaurus material in 2005, significantly improving understanding of the genus.
facts.quote: In 2005, a complete description was made by Le Loeuff of all known material, allowing Ampelosaurus to be much better understood.

facts.statement: A 2023 study by Vila and colleagues found that many bones previously assigned to Ampelosaurus actually belong to a distinct titanosaur, casting doubt on the assignment of isolated bones.
facts.quote: In 2023 however, examination of the material by Vila et al. revealed that many of the bones assigned to Ampelosaurus belong to a distinct titanosaur making it uncertain the assignment of isolated bones to either of these two species.

facts.statement: The scapula of Ampelosaurus was found attached to a coracoid and measured 72 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The scapula was found attached to a coracoid. In the longer direction, the bone is 72 cm long.

facts.statement: A pubis bone measuring about 75 centimeters in length has been identified in Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus is also known from a pubis, about 75 cm long.

facts.statement: Approximately 27 femora have been found at Bellevue, making them the most common bone type, with most being more or less complete.
facts.quote: About 27 femora are known from Bellevue, making them the most common bone, most of them more-or-less complete.

facts.statement: A study of bone physiology revealed a maximum femur length of 1,100 millimeters, which is significantly larger than the previously known maximum of 802 millimeters.
facts.quote: In a study of its bone physiology, it was found that the maximum known femur length was 1100 mm, which is much larger than previously known (802 mm).

facts.statement: The humeri of Ampelosaurus were robust, approximately 63 centimeters long, with highly expanded ends at both the distal and proximal regions.
facts.quote: The humeri are robust, about 63 cm long, with very expanded distal and proximal ends.

facts.statement: Two osteoderms with large spines were uncovered, each featuring a base about 12 centimeters tall with two large foramina.
facts.quote: Two with large spines have been uncovered. At the base of each spine, which is about 12 cm tall, are two large foramina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ampelosaurus atacis consists of a group of three connected dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of A. atacis is a group of three connected dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Ampelosaurus are opisthocoelous, characterized by centra that lengthen toward the rear.
facts.quote: The vertebrae are opisthocoelous, with centra that lengthen toward the rear.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Ampelosaurus possess an internal spongy structure containing very large cells.
facts.quote: The vertebrae also have an internal structure that is spongy, with very large cells.

facts.statement: Two poorly preserved sacral vertebrae found at Bellevue are believed to belong to a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: Two sacral vertebrae were known from Bellevue. They are poorly preserved, and are thought to belong to a juvenile.

facts.statement: Le Loeuff identified several distinguishing features for Ampelosaurus, including weakly spatulate teeth, laterally widening neural spine extremities, a strongly rear-inclining neural arch, a lack of distal scapular expansion, a ventral scapular crest, and plate, bulb, and spine-shaped osteoderms.
facts.quote: This set of characters was identified by Le Loeuff in his description of Ampelosaurus to distinguish it from all other genera: teeth that weakly spatulate; a laterally widening distal extremity of neural spines on the dorsal vertebrae; neural arch of the dorsal vertebrae inclining strongly towards the rear; the lack of a distal expansion on the scapular blade; the presence of a light, ventral crest on top of the scapula; the presence of plate, bulb, and spine shaped osteoderms; and, in 2005, Le Loeuff added that the constriction of the neural spine on the dorsal and cervical vertebrae was also probably a characteristic of Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2018, Díez Díaz and colleagues placed Ampelosaurus in the clade Lirainosaurinae, grouping it with other French and Spanish titanosaurs from the late Campanian to Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: More recently, Ampelosaurus has been put in a clade with other French and Spanish titanosaurs from the late Campanian to Maastrichtian, which was named Lirainosaurinae by Díez Díaz et al. in 2018.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ampelosaurus atacis have been discovered at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality in southern France.
facts.quote: Since 1989, over 500 bones discovered at the Upper Cretaceous Bellevue locality of southern France have been assigned to A. atacis.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is the sister taxon to Atsinganosaurus, and their shared clade is positioned phylogenetically between Saltasauridae and the groups Aeolosaurini or Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus nested as sister taxon to Atsinganosaurus also from France, and the entire clade was placed in between the taxa commonly classified as Saltasauridae and taxa normally in either Aeolosaurini or Lognkosauria.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest that many bones previously assigned to Ampelosaurus belong to a distinct species, potentially requiring the description of a new titanosaur and an emended diagnosis for Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: This study will lead to the erection of a new titanosaur species and to emended the diagnosis of Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus exhibited a slower growth rate after its bone microstructure became unique among sauropods.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus grew more slowly once the bone microstructure became unique among sauropods.

facts.statement: The onset of growth in Ampelosaurus was clearly delayed compared to other sauropods where it typically starts around sexual maturity.
facts.quote: The process of growing, which in other sauropods started around sexual maturity, was clearly delayed in Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: No growth marks have been found on any bone samples of Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus does not show growth marks on any bone sample.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus has not been found to possess EFS (External Fundamental System), a feature common in most non-titanosaurian sauropods.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus has not been known to have EFS, found on most non-titanosaurian sauropods.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Ampelosaurus might have had EFS because larger specimens were not tested in the study that reported its absence.
facts.quote: However, in the PLoS ONE study that found the lack of EFS, the larger specimens were not tested, so Ampelosaurus might have had EFS.

facts.statement: Most Ampelosaurus specimens show secondary osteons densely placed in the inner bone regions and lightly in the outer regions.
facts.quote: A majority of all Ampelosaurus specimens have been found with secondary osteons placed densely in the inner regions of bones, and lightly in outer regions.

facts.statement: No medullary cavity has been found in any bones of Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: Also, there is no medullary cavity in any bones of Ampelosaurus.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus atacis is definitively known only from the base of the Marnes de la Maurine Member in the Upper Aude Valley, southwestern France.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus atacis is only known with certainty at the base of the Marnes de la Maurine Member of the Marnes Rouges Inférieures Formation in the Upper Aude Valley in southwestern France (Aude department).

facts.statement: Magnetostratigraphic studies date the basal localities of Ampelosaurus to 71.5 million years ago, corresponding to the early Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Magnetostratigraphic studies indicate an age of 71.5 million years (top of chron C32n.1n) for the localities of the basal part of the Marnes de la Maurine Member (including the Bellevue locality), which corresponds to the early Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus roamed the plains of the Ibero-Armorican Island, a landmass comprising much of modern France and the Iberian Peninsula.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus roamed the vast plains of the Ibero-Armorican Island, an emergent landmass made up of much of the present day France and Iberian Peninsula.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of dinosaur eggshells and nests has been found in the Marnes de la Maurine Member where Ampelosaurus fossils occur.
facts.quote: Dinosaurs eggshells and nests are also present in the Marnes de la Maurine Member.

facts.statement: The macroflora at the Bellevue locality includes palm leaves, cycads, and angiosperm wood from trees 10 to 15 meters high.
facts.quote: The macroflora, notably found at Bellevue, is represented by leaves of palm trees and cycads, as well as fragments of angiosperm wood from trees 10 to 15 m high.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is classified as a moderate-sized titanosaur from the early Maastrichtian of southwestern France.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus (early Maastrichtian 71.5 Ma) from southwestern France (Aude department).

facts.statement: The genus Ampelosaurus was described by Le Loeuff in 1995.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Le Loeuff, 1995

facts.statement: The species A. atacis was described by Le Loeuff in 1995.
facts.quote: species_authority: Le Loeuff, 1995

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus belongs to the family Nemegtosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Nemegtosauridae

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is the only known species of the fossil genus Ampelosaurus, a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus atacis (gr."lagarto de Vid del río Aude") es la única especie conocida del género fósil Ampelosaurus de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió finales del Cretácico Superior, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Europa

facts.statement: The type species A. atacis was named by Le Loeuff in 1995.
facts.quote: Sus especie tipo es A. atacis, nombrado por Le Loeuff en 1995

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Ampelosaurus had long necks and tails, but it also possessed armor made of osteoderms.
facts.quote: Como todos los sauropodos, tenía cuello y cola largos, pero también una coraza con osteodermos

facts.statement: More than 500 bones have been assigned to Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: Más de 500 huesos han sido asignados a Ampelosaurus

facts.statement: A. atacis is known from a few well-preserved teeth and some cranial material.
facts.quote: De A. atacis se conoce unos pocos, bien conservados dientes y un poco de material craneal

facts.statement: A right scapula was discovered associated with a coracoid.
facts.quote: Una escápula derecha se descubrió asociado con un coracoides

facts.statement: Unlike most titanosaurs, the scapula blade of Ampelosaurus is triangular.
facts.quote: La hoja de la escápula, al contrario de la mayoría de los titanosaurios, es triangular

facts.statement: A. atacis is known from a pubis approximately 75 centimeters long and an ilium.
facts.quote: A. atacis también se conoce a partir de un pubis de aproximadamente 75 centímetros de largo y un ilion

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus likely had armor in the form of osteoderms ranging from 25 to 28 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los saurópodos, Ampelosaurus no solo habría tenido unos largo cuello y cola, sino que también lleva a la armadura en forma de osteodermos 25 a 28 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: This dinosaur would have measured about 15 meters from snout to tail.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio habría medido unos 15 metros desde el hocico hasta la cola

facts.statement: According to Gregory S. Paul, it averaged about 16 meters in length and weighed around 8000 kg.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Gregory S. Paul , media unos 16 metros de longitud y con un peso de alrededor de 8000 kg

facts.statement: It is considered a dwarf sauropod by Coria et al. (2005) because it has a smaller size compared to its ancestors.
facts.quote: Se considera que es un saurópodo enana por Coria et al. (2005), ya que tiene un tamaño más pequeño en comparación con sus antepasados

facts.statement: Since 1989, more than 500 bones discovered in the Bellevue locality in southern France have been assigned to A. atacis from the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Desde 1989, más de 500 huesos descubiertos en la localidad de Bellevue del sur de Francia han sido asignados a A. atacis perteneciente al Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus has teeth that are roughly cylindrical at the top with thin expansions at the bottom.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus tiene dientes que son más o menos cilíndricos en la parte superior con expansiones delgadas en la parte inferior

facts.statement: The teeth measure 21 millimeters high and about 6 millimeters wide.
facts.quote: Miden 21 milímetro de alto y unos 6 milímetros de ancho

facts.statement: The scapula is joined to the coracoid and measures 72 centimeters in its longest axis.
facts.quote: La escápula se encuentra unida al coracoides. En su eje más largo, el hueso mide 72 centímetros de largo

facts.statement: Unlike Magyarosaurus and Saltasaurus, the scapula lacks a dorsal crest at the base of the blade.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Magyarosaurus y Saltasaurus , la escápula no tiene la cresta dorsal en la base de la hoja escapular

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is also known from a pubis about 75 centimeters (30 inches) long.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus también se conoce a partir de un pubis , a unos 75 centímetros (30 pulgadas) de largo

facts.statement: The right ulna has a total length of 395 mm (15.6 inches).
facts.quote: El cúbito derecho tiene una longitud total de 395 mm (15,6 pulgadas

facts.statement: The left ulna is larger, with a length of 725 millimeters.
facts.quote: El cúbito izquierdo es más grande, con una longitud de 725 milímetros

facts.statement: Three different types of osteoderms have been recovered from Bellevue.
facts.quote: Tres tipos diferentes de osteodermos se han recuperado de Bellevue

facts.statement: Two types with large spines have been discovered; at the base of each column, about 12 centimeters high, are two large holes.
facts.quote: Dos con grandes espinas han sido descubiertas. En la base de cada columna, de unos 12 centímetros de altura, son dos grandes agujeros

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of A. atacis is a group of three connected dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de A. atacis es un grupo de tres vértebras dorsales conectados

facts.statement: The vertebrae are opisthocoelous, with centers that elongate toward the rear.
facts.quote: Las vértebras son opistocélicas, con centros que alargan hacia la parte trasera

facts.statement: The vertebrae also have a spongy internal structure with very large cells.
facts.quote: Las vértebras también tienen una estructura interna esponjosa, con celdas muy grandes

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus lived alongside many other animals, including over 8,500 specimens of gastropods, bivalves, crocodiles, other sauropods, plants, and invertebrates.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus vivió junto a muchos otros animales. Más de 8500 ejemplares se han encontrado junto a él, incluyendo gasterópodos, bivalvos, cocodrilos, otros saurópodos, las plantas y los invertebrados

facts.statement: It is debated whether there were at least two different titanosaurs in southern France during the Late Cretaceous, as another skull showed some differences.
facts.quote: Otro cráneo fue descrito del sur de Francia, pero mostró algunas diferencias, lo que significa que podría haber sido al menos dos titanosaurios diferentes en Francia a finales del Cretácico

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is distinguished by weakly spatulate teeth, laterodistal widening of neural spine tips, strongly posteriorly inclined dorsal neural arches, lack of distal scapula blade expansion, a light ventral crest on the scapula, and osteoderms shaped like plates, bulbs, and columns.
facts.quote: los dientes débilmente en forma de espátula, un ensanchamiento laterodistal de la extremidad de las espinas neurales en las vértebras dorsales, arco neural de las vértebras dorsales que se inclinan fuertemente hacia la parte trasera, la falta de una expansión distal de la lámina de la escápula, la presencia de una luz, ventral cresta en la parte superior de la escápula, la presencia de osteodermos en forma de placa, bulbo, y columna

facts.statement: In 2005, Le Loeuff suggested that constriction of the neural spine in dorsal and cervical vertebrae was likely also a characteristic of Ampelosaurus.
facts.quote: en 2005, Le Loeuff añadió que la constricción de la espina neural en el dorsal y cervical vértebras era probablemente también una característica de Ampelosaurus

facts.statement: The French paleontologist Jean Le Loeuff described and named this dinosaur in 1995.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo francés Jean Le Loeuff describió y nombró a este dinosaurio en 1995

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus fossils were recovered from the lower levels of the Marnes Rouges inférieures formation, dating to the early Maastrichtian to late Cretaceous, between 74 and 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue recuperado en los niveles más bajos de la formación Marnes Rouges inférieures, que pertenecen al maastrichtiano temprano a finales del Período Cretácico, hace entre 74 y 70 millones de años

facts.statement: The sediments where Ampelosaurus was found represent an ancient floodplain with numerous river channels.
facts.quote: Estos sedimentos representan una llanura inundable antigua con numerosos canales del río

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus was originally found near the commune of Campagne-sur-Aude in the Aude department, France.
facts.quote: Ampelosaurus fue encontrado originalmente cerca de la comuna de Campagne-sur-Aude en el departamento de Aude, Francia

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Greek words ampelos ("vine") and sauros ("lizard") because the original fossil remains were found near the Blanquette de Limoux vineyard in southern France.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico es derivado de las palabras griegas ampelos αμπελους ("vid") y sauros ("lagarto"), porque los restos fósiles originales fueron encontrados cerca de la viña de Blanquette de Limoux al sur de Francia

facts.statement: Only one species, A. atacis, has been described, and its specific name is due to the Aude river, which in Latin is Atax.
facts.quote: Solo se ha descrito una especie, A. atacis, su segundo nombre es debido al río Aude, que en latín es Atax

facts.statement: The first remains were found in a "bone bed" discovered in 1989, which yielded numerous ribs, back and tail vertebrae, many limb bones, but no skull material except for a tooth.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos fueron encontrados en una "cama de huesos" descubierto en 1989, que produjo numerosas costillas y vértebras de la espalda y la cola, así como muchos huesos de las extremidades, pero ningún material de cráneo aparte de un diente

facts.statement: Four osteoderms of different sizes and shapes were also recovered from this "bone bed".
facts.quote: Cuatro osteodermos de tamaños y formas diferentes que también fueron recobradas de esta "cama de huesos"

facts.statement: Later, in 2001, the Campagne-sur-Aude site was explored again by Gerard Chauvet, Jean-Luc Le Douarec, Colette Rives, and Yvonne Vidoux.
facts.quote: Más tarde, en 2001, el sitio de Campagne-sur-Aude fue explorado de nuevo, esta vez por Gerard Chauvet, Jean-Luc Le Douarec, Colette Rives e Yvonne Vidoux

facts.statement: After 13 years of searching, they discovered an almost complete skeleton containing much more material, including the previously unknown holotype bones.
facts.quote: Después de 13 años de búsqueda, habían descubierto un esqueleto casi completo que contenía mucho más material, incluidos los huesos desconocidos del holotipo

facts.statement: A new, undescribed species, A. sp., was discovered in 2007.
facts.quote: Una nueva especie, todavía sin describir, A. sp. fue descubierta en 2007

facts.statement: It was found during the construction of a high-speed railway connecting Madrid and Valencia, in a very rich fossil site located in the Sierra Villalba formation.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en el curso de la construcción de una vía férrea de alta velocidad que une Madrid con Valencia, en un yacimiento de fósiles muy rico que se encuentran en la formación de la Sierra Villalba

facts.statement: The site was located in a place called "Lo Hueco", near the town of Fuentes, in Castilla-La Mancha, Spain.
facts.quote: El sitio estaba en una localidad llamada "Lo Hueco", cerca de la población de Fuentes, Castilla-La Mancha, España

facts.statement: Over several months, an emergency large-scale excavation by more than 60 paleontologists and 100 manual workers allowed thousands of plant, invertebrate, and vertebrate specimens from the late Maastrichtian-early Campanian to be saved, including A. sp.
facts.quote: En el transcurso de varios meses, una excavación de gran escala de emergencia realizada por más de 60 paleontólogos y 100 trabajadores manuales permitió que miles de especímenes de plantas, invertebrados y vertebrados de finales del Maastrichtiano-Campaniano temprano puedan ser salvados, incluyendo A. sp.

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus belongs to the parent group Lirainosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lirainosaurinae

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Ampelosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Jean Le Loeuff published a more complete description of Ampelosaurus bones in 2005, which included a braincase and a right dentary.
rejected.quote: In 2005, Le Loeuff published a more complete description of the bones discovered since 1989 including a braincase and a right dentary.
